about.page.title: Our story
about.page.lead: Over 35 years of experience, research and commitment to sustainability in the field.
about.paragraph1: LIA AGRO has operated in Brazil for over 35 years. Its German founders brought knowledge and experience to Brazil, which led to the ROCKSIL® PLUS and PROTEGO FL technologies.
about.paragraph2: ROCKSIL® PLUS is a mineral input used in different crops and crop-management systems in Brazil. The experience gained contributed to the company’s expansion into international markets.
about.paragraph3: With PROTEGO FL, LIA AGRO also operates in fruit and vegetable washing and preservation, serving market vendors, restaurants and food-processing industries.
about.export: A pioneer in exporting agricultural inputs for conventional and organic farming, LIA AGRO expanded from Brazil into European and Asian markets, building commercial relationships with international partners.

about.founder.p1: The founder of LIA AGRO, while still young in Germany, suffered DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) poisoning. DDT was the first modern synthetic organochlorine pesticide, widely used from the Second World War onward to control disease vectors and agricultural pests.
about.founder.intro: It was then that a question arose:
about.founder.quote: Who has the right to poison our food!?
about.founder.p2: At that time, Rachel Carson’s book “Silent Spring”, published in 1962, was already available in libraries and served as a warning about the paths along which science might lead the world!
about.founder.p3: Among the great pioneers of this science was the German Dr. Justus von Liebig, regarded as the father of modern agricultural chemistry and one of those responsible for the development of mineral fertilization.
about.founder.p4: His contemporary, Dr. Julius Hensel, author of “Bread from Stones”, argued that rock powders could produce effects comparable to those of chemical fertilizers without causing imbalances in the environment and, consequently, in plants.
about.founder.p5: At that time, attention focused mainly on the rapid growth and increased size of plants resulting from the application of chemical fertilizers. However, insufficient attention was paid to possible consequences for plant metabolism. Among them was nutritional imbalance, which could favor the accumulation of free amino acids, making plants more susceptible to attack by different pathogens.
about.founder.p6: LIA AGRO has operated in Brazil for over 35 years, aiming to contribute to the transition from conventional farming practices to integrated and sustainable management systems. This sector represents most of Brazilian agriculture and urgently needs alternative technologies that make it possible to safely reduce the use of agrochemicals, whose consumption places Brazil among the world’s largest users.
about.founder.p7: Another equally important objective is to support the growth of organic agriculture by offering solutions that make it possible to replace or reduce the use of copper-based products, whose use has been restricted by international regulations.
about.founder.p8: LIA AGRO learned from past experiences and observations in Germany and began researching, developing and testing minerals and their combinations. This work gave rise to ROCKSIL® PLUS and PROTEGO FL, products that have served its customers in Brazil, Europe and Asia for decades.
about.founder.p9: ROCKSIL® PLUS is used to treat plants in home gardens, small rural properties and large farms. PROTEGO FL serves market vendors, restaurants and food-processing businesses.
about.founder.p10: Those who learn to use our products correctly become loyal LIA AGRO customers, valuing a partnership built over the years in which both parties share the same goal:
rocksil.doc.intro.title: About the product
rocksil.doc.intro.p1: ROCKSIL is a fine powder obtained by grinding, micronizing and standardizing selected clays from Brazilian deposits, as described in the company’s technical material.
rocksil.doc.intro.p2: It disperses readily in water and adheres well to plant surfaces. According to the technical document, uptake takes approximately two hours. It is intended for preventive foliar application throughout the growing cycle.
rocksil.doc.intro.p3: The document reports field experience in vegetables, fruit, grapes, coffee, grains and ornamentals, associating ROCKSIL applications with plant vitality and induced resistance.
rocksil.doc.intro.p4: The material presents ROCKSIL as an alternative to help reduce agrochemical use in conventional management and copper-based products in organic farming, and reports effects on vegetative development and soluble solids (°Brix). Claims must be assessed for each crop and applicable regulations.
rocksil.doc.base.title: Raw materials
rocksil.doc.base.p1: The relationship between people and clay, stone and crushed rock is as old as civilization. Clay has long been used for utensils, storage and early writing.
rocksil.doc.base.p2: The document highlights the more recent use of rock powders in soil nutrition and conditioning, as well as the ability of some clays to retain water and interact with molecules.
rocksil.doc.base.p3: Based on these characteristics, LIA AGRO developed a powdered mineral blend intended for preventive foliar applications.
rocksil.doc.elements.title: Elements present
rocksil.doc.element.si: Silicon can help form physical barriers in plant tissues, supporting mechanical strength and reducing water loss under certain conditions.
rocksil.doc.element.s: Sulfur is essential to living organisms and forms part of important amino acids.
rocksil.doc.element.mg: Magnesium forms part of chlorophyll and is essential to photosynthesis.
rocksil.doc.element.ca: Calcium is involved in cellular signaling and various physiological and enzymatic functions.
rocksil.doc.element.ti: Titanium occurs naturally in minerals and clays, as described in the document.
rocksil.doc.element.fe: Iron is involved in metabolic processes related to chlorophyll formation and enzyme activity.

rocksil.doc.prep.lead: Mix the powder with part of the water to form a paste, then add the remaining water and mix until the dispersion is homogeneous.

rocksil.doc.crops.title: Application guidelines by crop
rocksil.doc.crops.lead: Mixing rates and intervals reproduced from the LIA AGRO technical document. Consult current technical guidance before application.
rocksil.doc.crop.tomato.detail: Substrate treatment: mix 250 g of ROCKSIL into each 25 kg of substrate. Omit this treatment when using biological control. Seeds: mix ROCKSIL powder at 0.5% (0.5 kg per 100 kg of seeds). Mix thoroughly so all seeds come into contact with the product. Omit this treatment if biological control is chosen. Seedling treatment: spray ROCKSIL at 0.5%–1% every four days. Make the last application one day before transplanting. For sensitive leafy crops, always use the lower concentration (e.g., iceberg lettuce).
rocksil.doc.crop.tomato.field: Field: begin weekly ROCKSIL treatments immediately after transplanting, using a 1% aqueous solution. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, the concentration may be increased to 1.5% for sensitive leafy crops and to 2% for broccoli and kale, until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.orange.detail: Seedling treatment: spray ROCKSIL at 0.5%–1% every four days. Make the last application one day before transplanting.
rocksil.doc.crop.orange.field: Field: begin monthly treatments when new shoots emerge and continue applying through flowering until harvest. Make the final treatment immediately after pruning. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the intervals to 15 days until symptoms disappear. Use a 1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution, increasing to 1.5% under these conditions if needed.
rocksil.doc.crop.berries.detail: Seedling treatment: spray ROCKSIL at 0.5% every four days. Make the last application one day before transplanting.
rocksil.doc.crop.berries.field: Field: begin weekly ROCKSIL treatments immediately after transplanting. Use an aqueous solution at 0.5%–1%.
rocksil.doc.crop.grape.detail: Field: begin weekly ROCKSIL treatments as plants emerge from dormancy, with the final application immediately after pruning. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the intervals to four days until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.grape.field: Application concentration: use a 1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, the concentration may be increased to 1.5% until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.coffee.detail: Seedlings: begin ROCKSIL treatments at 0.5% every two weeks.
rocksil.doc.crop.coffee.field: Field: begin monthly treatments as plants emerge from dormancy, with the last application immediately after pruning. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the interval to 15 days until symptoms disappear. Use a 1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution, increasing to 1.5% under these conditions if needed.
rocksil.doc.crop.soy.detail: Field: begin ROCKSIL treatments immediately after emergence, every 21 days. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the interval to 15 days until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.soy.field: Application concentration: use a 1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, the concentration may be increased to 1.5% until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.corn.detail: Field: begin ROCKSIL treatments immediately after emergence, every 21 days. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the interval to 15 days until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.corn.field: Application concentration: use a 1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, the concentration may be increased to 1.5% until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.ornamental.detail: Field or greenhouse: begin weekly ROCKSIL treatments at the seedling stage and continue throughout the plant’s growing cycle. Make the last treatment shortly before cutting. Under climatic stress (rainy weather) or when diseases appear, shorten the intervals to three days until symptoms disappear.
rocksil.doc.crop.ornamental.field: Application concentration: use a 0.5%–1% aqueous ROCKSIL solution.
rocksil.doc.crops.common.title: Notes, incompatibilities and compatibilities
rocksil.doc.crops.common: ROCKSIL is absorbed by plants in approximately two hours, so another application is not necessary if it rains after that period. No spreading or sticking agent is needed, and no withholding period is stated. It is a contact product and should be applied regularly throughout the growing cycle to achieve its full potential. Always use clean water and clean equipment, free from residues of foreign substances. It is incompatible with alkaline substances (e.g., Bordeaux mixture) and organophosphate-based insecticides, which may harm the plants and reduce its effectiveness. It may be used together with biofertilizers and amino acids.
